version.changelog:
SafeShrink 1.2.12

- Updated contact QR code links in the user feedback/contact section.
- Updated version information to v1.2.12 and related metadata.
- Removed redundant documentation file (skill-card.md).

llm.summary: SafeShrink appears to be a real document-compression and sanitization skill, but it asks agents to auto-download and run a proprietary Windows EXE while also claiming fully offline operation.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose of compressing, sanitizing, OCRing, and converting documents is coherent with the described CLI commands and file outputs, and no artifact shows data upload, credential theft, or destructive behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad triggers for common file types and document requests, instructs active interception of normal file handling, and claims its interception rules take priority over other skills, which is overbroad for a document utility.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md says the AI will automatically download and cache a GitHub ZIP/EXE on first use, but elsewhere repeatedly says the tool is fully offline and no internet is needed. The executable is proprietary/compiled and no hash or signature verification is provided.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Processing sensitive documents locally is purpose-aligned, but the artifacts encourage antivirus whitelisting and assert false positives while relying on a downloaded binary, which needs stronger disclosure and verification.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The only persistence described is local caching of the EXE and generated output files; there is no evidence of background service installation, drivers, system-file modification, or credential/session use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want SafeShrink to mediate document handling and are comfortable with a proprietary Windows EXE downloaded from GitHub. Review the download source yourself, avoid automatic execution without consent, do not assume sanitized/OCR output is safe to share without inspection, and be cautious about adding the whole tool folder to antivirus exclusions.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as material: the offline/no-internet privacy framing conflicts with automatic download and caching of an executable from GitHub.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted as material for the EXE download concern: fetching and caching a proprietary binary is not clearly gated by explicit informed consent or integrity verification.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: file-extension and passive-language triggers are broad enough to route unrelated document workflows into this skill, especially with its active-interception instructions.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded for OCR/image-output leakage: OCR and embedded images are expected for this tool, but users should be warned that converted or sanitized files may still contain sensitive content.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted for the manifest trigger concern because _meta.json repeats generic file extensions and common document-processing terms that can broaden activation.
